:::{#def-finite-set}
#### Finite set, infinite set, and cardinality

A set $A$ is **finite**
if it is empty,
or if, for some natural number $n$,
its elements can be listed as a finite sequence (@def-sequence) $a_1, \ldots, a_n$
in which each element of $A$ appears exactly once.
That number $n$ is the **cardinality** of $A$, its number of elements,
written $\abs{A}$;
the empty set has cardinality $\abs{\emptyset} = 0$.

A set that is not finite is **infinite**.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-cardinality-bars}
#### Two meanings of $\abs{\cdot}$

Applied to a set, the bars $\abs{A}$ mean the cardinality of $A$.
Applied to a number, $\abs{x}$ means its
[absolute value](algebra.qmd#def-absolute-value),
or its [modulus](algebra.qmd#def-complex-modulus) when $x$ is complex.
For example, $\abs{\set{-3}} = 1$, but $\abs{-3} = 3$.

:::
